ops.task_class: new measurement tool + its golden tests
ops.statement: When a measurement/lint tool and its golden-fixture tests are built in separate gates, enumerate the tool's finding status/check vocabulary as a closed set in a shared contract both read — otherwise the test gate reverse-engineers the exact strings from the tool source (a g1/g3 seam guess).
ops.grounding: issue-104 G1 + G3 crew Workflow Feedback: G1 left status vocab (flagged/shortlist/info/ok) implied-in-prose; G3 had to source the exact strings from curate_corpus.py to assert on them.

ops.task_class: authoring a skill/doc under a self-check budget
ops.statement: A handoff that requires an authored artifact to pass its own dogfood/self-check budget (e.g. a word-count heuristic) AND to cover a fixed list of topics must name the budget-vs-content tension explicitly, so the author writes tight from the first draft rather than trimming down after a failed dogfood run.
ops.grounding: issue-104 G2 crew Workflow Feedback: curator SKILL.md had to cover 8 body topics and pass curate_corpus's 400-word size budget; the tension was unflagged and cost several trim passes (818->400 words).
ops.target: IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF template note on self-check budgets

ops.task_class: detector + fixes by one author (T5 acceptance)
ops.statement: For a detector whose author also wrote the fixes, pair the mechanical detector run with an independent fresh-context sweep given NEITHER the script NOR the fix list. Convergence on the finding set validates the detector isn't self-confirming; the independent sweep's pointer-vs-doctrine semantic judgment is exactly the value a mechanical (T7) detector cannot supply itself.
ops.grounding: issue-104 G5 ACCEPTANCE_NOTE: curate_corpus and the independent sonnet sweep converged on the same duplication clusters; the only differences were semantic pointer-vs-doctrine calls the script deliberately does not make.
ops.target: curator SKILL.md acceptance doctrine / T5 pattern
